validation_rules: A latest pointer is valid only when trading_day and run_state_path match the current ET date and the expected stream root.

A date-specific same-day run_state file is preferred over the latest pointer when both are present.
A pending same-day placeholder has valid_scheduled_evidence=false until the target run_state exists AND has run_origin='scheduled' and manual_run=false.
valid_scheduled_evidence is derived from the target run_state, never asserted blindly by the pointer.

spread_gate_outcome_contract_2026_07_27.incident: The 1:30 PM ET intraday run recorded error_class='missing_spread_data' on a run where no ticker had qualified on the ladder at all, so nothing ever reached the spread gate and the missing spread was irrelevant to the outcome. A healthy zero-order run was recorded as a data failure.
spread_gate_outcome_contract_2026_07_27.evaluation_order: Evaluate the ladder and same-day top-up rules FIRST, then the spread gate. Only candidates that qualify reach the gate, and only rows that reach the gate carry a spread verdict.

no_candidates_before_spread_gate.condition: No ticker qualifies, so no candidate ever reaches the spread gate.
no_candidates_before_spread_gate.note: A normal, healthy zero-order run. It MUST NOT record error_class='missing_spread_data', MUST NOT be recorded as a trading failure or a missed slot, and MUST NOT count as an error in scheduled reliability.

blocked_before_the_spread_gate.condition: Tickers DID qualify on the ladder and top-up rules, but every one was stopped by a budget, cap, per-order ceiling, already-bought-today, or same-day-duplicate check that runs BEFORE the spread lookup, so none carries a spread verdict.
blocked_before_the_spread_gate.note: Distinguished from no_ladder_candidates by the CANDIDATE count, not the spread-gate count. Recording it as no_ladder_candidates would claim the ladder produced nothing when it did.

placement_attempted_and_failed.condition: Qualifying candidates reached placement and every attempt raised.
placement_attempted_and_failed.note: A zero-order run is not automatically a healthy one. A run whose placements all raised is a genuine failure and MUST NOT be recorded as completed_no_orders. The complete artifact set is still written.

raised_before_reaching_placement.condition: The run raised before placement was attempted at all: a startup failure, a data failure, or an account lookup failure.
raised_before_reaching_placement.note: Deliberately distinct from failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt, which means placement WAS attempted. Reporting keyed on the placement outcome would otherwise misattribute a startup or data failure as a broker-placement failure.

blocked_before_placement.condition: A precondition or wiring gate stopped the run before placement: no same-day pre-flight artifact, no broker adapter, the wrong live account, or a raw-input persistence failure.
blocked_before_placement.note: These paths write and return before the run's normal classification step, so each stamps these fields itself. A more specific error_class the path already set, such as missing_or_invalid_raw_inputs, is kept.

failed_after_submitting.condition: The run raised AFTER at least one order was accepted by the broker.
failed_after_submitting.note: The aggregate fields MUST NOT contradict orders_submitted_count and the submitted_orders.csv rows. A run that failed after placing an order did submit; recording not_submitted_error there would let a summary consumer report no submission while the CSV holds the order. The retained outcomes also carry placement_evidence_incomplete=true: they are a floor on what was placed, never proof nothing else was.

manual_placement_failure.condition: A MANUAL run's broker placement failed.
manual_placement_failure.note: The manual path never runs the scheduled connector-native recovery policy, so its broker failures MUST NOT be recorded as failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt or reporting keyed on that outcome misattributes them as failed scheduled recovery attempts.

concrete_status_precedence.rule: A concrete terminal order_submit_status the placement path produced always survives the no-order classification.
concrete_status_precedence.note: Replacing not_submitted_confirmation_required with the generic no-order status would make is_confirmation_blocked() return false and lose the fact that broker confirmation is pending. Only the not_submitted_budget_exhausted catch-all is replaced, and only when no candidate was really blocked on a budget, cap, or buying-power check.

degraded_market_data.condition: The run completed with zero orders while one or more market-data providers were raising, so its tickers degraded to NO_DATA or manual review rather than being genuinely evaluated.
sources: A market-data provider that raised. The runner catches it and degrades the ticker to a NO_DATA signal carrying a 'provider error' warning, so that ticker was never genuinely evaluated.
A pre-placement broker check that raised (same-day order lookup, tradability, review), recorded as a NON-deliberate block. A deliberate safety gate carries deliberate_skip=true and is not an error.
degraded_market_data.note: A zero-order run with errors_count > 0 is NOT a clean ladder no-op and MUST NOT be recorded with a null error_class, or a summary or reliability consumer reads a data-failure run as healthy. A concrete spread cause is more specific and takes precedence.

row_blocking_gate_attribution.rule: A row counts toward candidates_blocked_missing_spread ONLY when the spread gate itself blocked it, recorded on the row as blocked_by='spread_gate'.
row_blocking_gate_attribution.must_not: MUST NOT infer a spread block from spread_status alone. A manual run does not fail closed on an unproven spread, so a row can carry spread_status='spread_unavailable' and still be stopped later by human review or broker confirmation, which is not a spread-caused outcome.

all_candidates_blocked_at_spread_gate.condition: Candidates qualified and reached the gate, and EVERY one was failed closed because its bid/ask spread could not be proven.
all_candidates_blocked_at_spread_gate.note: Still a safe no-order skip and still valid scheduled evidence that the slot executed. The complete artifact set is written.

partially_unavailable.condition: Some qualifying rows have a proven spread and others do not.
partially_unavailable.required_behavior: Fail ONLY the unproven rows closed, recording spread_ok=false and spread_status='spread_unavailable' (no bid/ask captured) or 'spread_not_ok' (captured but outside tolerance) on those rows, and continue evaluating and submitting every other qualifying row that passes every check.
must_not: MUST NOT abort the whole run because spread is missing or bad for a subset of tickers.
MUST NOT suppress an otherwise-qualifying ticker whose own spread was proven because a different ticker's spread was unavailable.
MUST NOT place an order for a ticker whose spread could not be proven.

spread_gate_outcome_contract_2026_07_27.not_evaluated_note: A row that never reached the gate records spread_status='not_evaluated' and is never counted as blocked for a missing spread. It is never recorded as spread_ok=true.
spread_gate_outcome_contract_2026_07_27.never: Spread inputs are never estimated, inferred, or defaulted. A ticker with unproven spread is skipped, not approximated.
spread_gate_outcome_contract_2026_07_27.enforced_by: scripts/run_classification.py: spread_gate_fields stamps the per-row verdict and classify_no_order_run turns the two run-level counts into the recorded outcome. Both the morning/midday runner (morning_dca.py) and the afternoon runner (near_close_dca.py) route through them.

canonical_first_buy_and_topup_rule.title: JUL 24 2026 EXACT FIRST-BUY AND SAME-DAY TOP-UP RULE
canonical_first_buy_and_topup_rule.summary: Canonical per-ticker rule for selecting the first same-day buy base amount (before the ladder multiplier) and for governing later same-day top-ups. This is the source of truth; the code in near_close_dca.select_first_allocation_base_usd and near_close_dca.evaluate_top_up_guard, the morning mirror in morning_dca.py, and the base_selection_rule blocks in config/budgets.json and config/sizing_ladder.json all implement it, with one tracked exception -- see effective_prior_usd_gap_2026_07_24 below.

reason_strings.below_prior_close_and_low: First buy sized from the $2.00 base (base_amount_usd): current decision price is below BOTH yesterday's completed regular-session close AND low.
reason_strings.below_prior_close_only: First buy sized from the $1.00 base (base_amount_below_close_usd): current decision price is below yesterday's close but NOT below yesterday's low. A missing or unknown prior low is treated conservatively as not-below-low ($1.00).
reason_strings.not_below_prior_close_no_buy: No buy: current decision price is not below yesterday's close, or the active multiplier is 0.
reason_strings.same_day_topup_not_lower_or_no_delta: Skip a same-day top-up: current decision price is not strictly below this ticker's prior same-day buy reference, or corrected_delta_usd resolves to 0.

rules: 1. Apply this rule independently per ticker.

2. If a ticker has no same-day prior buy, fill, submitted order, valid order artifact, manual recovery fill, or broker-confirmed same-day context, treat the current evaluation as that ticker's first buy of the day.
3. For that first buy, compare the current decision price against yesterday's completed regular-session close AND yesterday's completed regular-session low for that ticker.
4. If the current price is lower than yesterday's close but NOT lower than yesterday's low, desired_usd = $1.00 x active multiplier (reason below_prior_close_only).
5. If the current price is lower than BOTH yesterday's close and yesterday's low, desired_usd = $2.00 x active multiplier (reason below_prior_close_and_low).
6. If the current price is not lower than yesterday's close, or the multiplier is 0, do not buy that ticker (reason not_below_prior_close_no_buy).
7. If there were no previous same-day buys for that ticker, always evaluate from yesterday's close and low; do not apply a same-day top-up blocker to a ticker with no prior same-day context.
8. Same-day buys in other tickers must never block a first allocation for this ticker.
9. If the ticker DOES have same-day prior buy context, ignore yesterday's low for that ticker and use that ticker's most recent valid same-day buy reference as the comparison reference.
10. For a subsequent same-day buy, buy again only when the current decision price is strictly lower than that ticker's prior same-day buy reference.
11. Recompute the desired allocation on the current active ladder, then buy only the difference: corrected_delta_usd = max(0, desired_usd - effective_prior_usd).
12. If the current price is not strictly lower than the same-day reference, or corrected_delta_usd is 0, skip that ticker with the concrete reason same_day_topup_not_lower_or_no_delta.
13. If same-day context cannot be resolved for one ticker, perform one bounded same-day context reload, then fail only that ticker closed without blocking other tickers.

canonical_first_buy_and_topup_rule.per_ticker_independence: Every ticker resolves its own same-day context. failure_recovery_policy.recovery_trigger_note: A trigger only applies when the underlying market/account data was already fetched; the failure is in persisting, parsing, normalizing, or writing it, or in transient connector throttling. recovery_procedure: Rerun the required READ-ONLY inputs exactly once (no additional retries).
Persist all raw responses to disk FIRST, before any computation.
Recompute the run only from the persisted raw files (never from in-memory partial state).

Reuse the same logical scheduled run directory for the stream (market_open_dca/YYYYMMDD_0935ET/, morning_dca/YYYYMMDD_1030ET/, midday_dca/YYYYMMDD_1230ET/, intraday_dca/YYYYMMDD_<slot>ET/ for the fired slot, or scheduled_runs/YYYYMMDD_1530ET/) and stamp recovery_rerun=true on the run_state.

same_day_top_up_policy.summary: One same-day top-up guard governs the market-open (9:35), morning (10:30), intraday (11:30/1:30/2:30), midday (12:30), and afternoon (3:30) live streams AND manual override same-day fills. Each later run buys only the incremental difference max(0, desired_amount - prior_same_day_amount), and only when its current decision price is strictly below the prior same-day reference price; otherwise it buys $0. same_day_top_up_policy.broker_minimum_order_size: Added after the 2026-07-30/07-31 incident replay below documented a $0.50 DFTX resize (docs/dca_operational_todos.md, 'Broker minimum order size'). scripts.run_classification.incremental_top_up_amount rejects an incremental amount that is strictly positive but below the broker minimum (default $1.00, cent-quantized via Decimal to avoid float-subtraction false negatives at the boundary) and returns guard_result='below_broker_minimum_order_size' ($0, no order) instead of submitting an order the broker would reject. This narrows same_day_top_up_guard_enforcement_2026_07_31's 'policy unchanged' framing for amounts under the minimum: an incremental resize that the guard would otherwise have permitted is now blocked when it is below this floor. Every live path enforces the same floor because they all call the same helper.
same_day_top_up_policy.reference_price_preference: The prior same-day reference price is resolved in order: logged target_price, then decision_price, then average_fill_price (from orders.csv or a manual override's filled_orders.csv). A missing reference price (none available) means NO automatic top-up: the candidate is classified execution_status='manual_review_candidate' (top_up_manual_review=true) at $0.

It buys again only when the final decision price is strictly lower than that most recent reference, and then buys only corrected_delta_usd = max(0, desired_usd - effective_prior_usd). A missing prior reference => no auto-top-up.

If the aggregate remainder for a ticker is greater than or equal to $0.50 and less than $1.00, round up and buy exactly $1.00, subject to the normal caps and safety checks.

Only remainders blocked by Robinhood's minimum order size qualify. Do not convert unrelated spread, confidence, budget, duplicate, tradability, or top-up price-reference blocks into minimum-order round-ups.

scheduled_run_outcomes.collection_contract: Every row is a scheduled-stream outcome for its slot (run_origin='scheduled'), so a consumer may aggregate fills, reliability, and cost metrics across runs[] without a second per-row filter. rules: Compute the budget tier BEFORE order placement using SOLELY the count of 3x-or-greater signals in the full actionable incremental plan -- never planned spend, which is an output of the sizing decision, not an input fixed before it.
Normal tier: 3x-or-greater signals <= 5, corrected daily cap $180.
Elevated tier: 3x-or-greater signals 6 to 10, corrected daily cap $240.
High-volatility tier: 3x-or-greater signals 11 to 17, corrected daily cap $300.
Stress tier: 3x-or-greater signals > 17, corrected daily cap $360 only to the extent unused weekly rollover reserve is available.

Count same-day strategy allocation already placed in manual recovery, morning, midday, and earlier final orders as corrected-daily-cap usage for safety, while keeping the streams separate for evidence and slippage.

If planned spend (in dollars) exceeds the remaining corrected daily capacity of the tier SELECTED above, rank the remaining eligible orders by deepest drop percentage, then multiplier, then amount, place only the orders that fit the remaining cap and the per-order $15 max, and write budget_blocked.csv plus per-symbol block_reason='budget_block_corrected_daily_cap' for the rest.

If a budget-logic inconsistency is detected after any order has already been placed, recover inside the same scheduled run directory (scheduled_runs/YYYYMMDD_1530ET/), reconcile the already placed orders, apply the corrected cap logic, and finalize state rather than escalating without complete artifacts.

The order was created INSIDE the true final-run scheduled UTC window -- at or after 19:30Z AND at or before 19:35Z during EDT -- AND is not already claimed by an earlier stream artifact.

Any order created before the true final-run window opens.

It is ALSO cross-referenced in recovery_and_escalation_runs, noting recovery_rerun=true and the trigger reason, satisfying the requirement that every same-day recovery appear there; that cross-reference counts toward recovery_and_escalation_count (which tracks recovery/escalation EVENTS broadly) but not toward run_count_recovery or run_count_scheduled again. run_count_recovery is reserved for a recovery that is its own separate run/artifact, distinct from the slot's own retry: e.g. a parent recovery submission, a subagent escalation, or a manual override recorded under its own manual_recovery/manual_runs path.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.manual_recovery_classification_rule: A manual recovery's classification is read from its OWN source artifact, not assumed from being a recovery. missed_morning_run_recovery_policy and midday_dca_manual_recovery_2026_07_20 both stamp same_day_top_up_context_only=true and valid_scheduled_evidence=false on their manual recovery artifacts: those runs are classified top_up_context_only, matching the source, not manual_context_only. manual_context_only is reserved for a manual run whose source artifact is NOT marked same_day_top_up_context_only=true (e.g. a manual dry run or diagnostic that participates in no same-day guard). Relabeling a same_day_top_up_context_only=true artifact as manual_context_only would contradict the source and lose the distinction top_up_context_only exists to preserve.

per_run_field_rules.run_id: Exact run id as written in the artifact. If a run failed before writing any artifact, record 'no_run_id_written' plus the expected id it would have used.
per_run_field_rules.stream: One of market_open, watchlist, preflight, morning, intraday, midday, afternoon, slippage, watchdog, or recovery. slippage (not post_trade) matches the value the 67aa802b post-trade task's own model-usage directory entry and same_day_pointer_validation_policy already persist -- codex review discussion_r3657657882. preflight matches bb4f6ef1's separately-logged preflight sub-invocation (see model_usage_log.applies_to_daily_tasks_et stream_note).
per_run_field_rules.triggering_issue: For scheduled runs this is 'scheduled'. For everything in the recovery section this is the concrete failure or gap that caused the run, not a generic label.
per_run_field_rules.order_attempts: Count of order placement ATTEMPTS recorded in the artifact, with fills if recorded. Read from persisted artifacts only. This report never calls a broker and never reviews orders.
per_run_field_rules.connector_calls: Count of connector or provider pulls only where they were actually logged. notification_count is sourced the same way, from usage_proxy.notifications_sent.  Where not logged, write 'not_logged' rather than estimating. The persisted source is the run's own usage_proxy.finance_calls_attempted plus usage_proxy.robinhood_calls_attempted (near_close_dca.build_usage_proxy); connector_pull_count_where_logged sums these over exactly the runs that recorded them, which is what 'where_logged' scopes it to -- a run lacking that telemetry is out of scope, not an unknown that voids the total. Only when NO covered run persisted a connector count is the counter 'not_logged' and the connector_load band 'not_available'; a fabricated 0/low is never emitted -- codex review discussion_r3659298016.
per_run_field_rules.model_usage_rows: Count of appended rows for this run in model_usage/YYYYMM/model_usage.jsonl, but ONLY when at least one row for this exact run_id is found: in that case write the exact matching count (normally 1). If NO row matches this run_id -- whether because the model_usage/YYYYMM/model_usage.jsonl file itself is absent, OR the file exists (other runs logged successfully) but has no row for this specific run -- do NOT write 0: write 'not_available' with a one-line reason, per unavailable_data_rule. scripts/model_usage_log.py's log_model_usage() is deliberately best-effort and silently swallows its own append failures (unknown task, bad entry, disk error) so a run's own logging bug can never break that run; a missing row for one run therefore never proves zero usage, and treating it as 0 could hide a premium-routed run and understate model_load -- codex review discussion_r3658096711.
per_run_field_rules.classification: Exactly one of valid_scheduled_evidence, top_up_context_only, manual_context_only, failed_start_no_evidence, or did_not_run.

credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.failed_start_no_evidence_rule: A scheduled run that was ATTEMPTED and failed before writing any artifact (run_id='no_run_id_written') is classified failed_start_no_evidence. It is never classified valid_scheduled_evidence (no artifact exists to serve as evidence) and never top_up_context_only or manual_context_only (it is neither a top-up input nor a manual run). Its one full per-run record (with all per_run_required_fields populated) lives in the recovery_and_escalation_runs section, and it alone counts toward recovery_and_escalation_count and error_count.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.failed_start_scheduled_slot_rule: This case must appear in BOTH sections, but only ONCE as a substantive record. must_cover_active_daily_chain requires the id to appear in scheduled_runs; failed_start_no_evidence_rule requires its only real record to live in recovery_and_escalation_runs. Resolve this by making the scheduled_runs row a CROSS-REFERENCE only: classification='failed_start_no_evidence', run_id='no_run_id_written', triggering_issue='see recovery_and_escalation_runs', and every other per_run_required_field (stream is the one exception -- always populated, since it identifies which slot the cross-reference is for) set to the literal string 'cross_reference_only' rather than a real measurement -- codex review discussion_r3658096697. This cross-reference row is not counted again: it does not add to run_count_scheduled, recovery_and_escalation_count, or error_count, since those are already incremented once by the row's real record in the recovery section. did_not_run does not apply here because it means no attempt occurred at all, which is not the case for an attempted-and-failed start.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.did_not_run_rule: A scheduled slot that never fired at all (no attempt was made: the scheduler never triggered it, it was gated out, or it is simply absent from the day's artifacts, as distinct from an attempted-and-failed start) is classified did_not_run, with run_id='not_applicable_did_not_run' plus the concrete reason in triggering_issue. It is recorded in the scheduled_runs section (per active_daily_chain_note, every one of the eight active ids must appear even with no run) and does NOT count toward recovery_and_escalation_count or error_count, since no attempt occurred to recover from or error on.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.did_not_run_vs_failed_start_evidence_rul: An empty run directory alone cannot distinguish 'never triggered' from 'triggered and crashed before writing anything' (Codex review: 'Persist evidence that distinguishes failed starts from missed slots' -- Slack alerts and heartbeat pings are external, fire-and-forget calls with no local trace). dca_alerts.guarded_run now closes this for the streams it wraps: on an escaping exception it calls dca_alerts.write_failed_start_marker(stream, exc), persisting a durable local record under attempt_log/YYYYMMDD/<stream>.json (see data_sources). The report reads that marker FIRST: if a same-day marker exists for a slot with no run directory, classify failed_start_no_evidence (using the marker's error_class/error_message as triggering_issue) per failed_start_scheduled_slot_rule; only when neither a run directory nor a marker exists is the slot did_not_run. Failure phase: not every escaping exception is a failed START -- a scheduled run can persist a valid run_state.json and only then raise (the supported generate_full_reports=true path fails after run_daily_compact() has written the run), so each marker records failure_phase='before_run_artifact' (the genuine failed start) or 'after_run_artifact' (an ordinary late error on a run that completed its artifact). Only the former is classified failed_start_no_evidence; a late-phase marker becomes that run's own recorded_error, so it still counts toward error_count without fabricating an earlier failed start plus a successful retry, which would inflate the recovery/error counters and force error_load high for a run that did its work -- codex review discussion_r3659298031. A marker with no failure_phase field at all (written before the field existed) is read as a failed start, preserving prior behavior. Coverage note: guarded_run wraps the in-repo Python entrypoints for 42173154 (morning), a6239dae (midday, inherits MorningDCAExecutor.run()), 10ce362c (afternoon, via run_dca.py), and, as of 2026-08-03, 2ba19526 (market-open, MarketOpenDCAExecutor.run() inherits the same guarded_run wrapper) and 7be82b97 (intraday, IntradayDCAExecutor.run() likewise) -- both now write a durable attempt_log marker on an escaping exception the same way morning does. bb4f6ef1 (both sub-invocations) has no_python_entry_point=true -- the external scheduler/agent invokes it directly, so no in-repo code exists to write a marker for it -- and 67aa802b/a46bf007 are read-only consumers of other tasks' artifacts. For those three, an attempted-and-crashed invocation genuinely remains indistinguishable from a missed slot from this repo's own artifacts; the report states this limitation explicitly in caveats for any of those three classified did_not_run, rather than silently assuming a clean miss.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.counts_rule: Every counter is derived from persisted same-day artifacts and logs. A counter that cannot be measured is reported as 'not_logged' or 'not_available' with a one-line reason. Counters are never estimated, inferred, or backfilled from expectation. artifact_bytes_approx is explicitly approximate and is rounded, for example to the nearest KB.
credit_usage_proxy_report_2026_07_27.recovery_counter_membership_rule: recovery_and_escalation_count is the total number of ROWS in recovery_and_escalation_runs: one row per distinct artifact found across every type in recovery_artifact_types (recovery_artifact_types_rule already requires a type with nothing found to contribute 0, never be omitted). run_count_recovery is the subset of those rows that represent an actual additional EXECUTION with its own run_id: every recovery_artifact_types value counts toward it EXCEPT failed_scheduled_start (by definition zero successful execution -- see failed_start_no_evidence_rule) and subagent_escalation (a delegation/escalation event, not the executor's own additional run). Deduplication: a single underlying artifact is one row under whichever recovery_artifact_types label is most specific to it (e.g. a recovery rerun that is also a retry is filed once, as scheduled_recovery_attempt or same_day_recovery_run, not listed again under retry) -- it is never counted twice into either counter for matching more than one type description. recovery_run_count_by_stream (see recovery_counts_by_stream_rule) must sum to recovery_and_escalation_count, not run_count_recovery, since it breaks down every row including failed_scheduled_start/subagent_escalation rows -- codex review discussion_r3658096704.

proxy_bands.unavailable_band_rule: If the counter(s) a dimension's band is derived from are reported not_logged or not_available (source absent) for one or more covered runs, that dimension's band is reported not_available with the same reason, never guessed, defaulted to low, or omitted. This applies in particular to model_load when model_usage/YYYYMM/model_usage.jsonl itself is absent (see model_usage_rows rule) and to connector_load or error_load when a run's counter is not_logged.
proxy_bands.exact_credits_rule: Exact Perplexity credit totals are not exposed. The report states a band plus the measurable proxy value behind it. It must not print an exact credit count, an estimated credit count, a dollar cost, or any billing figure, and must not imply one by arithmetic.

The band is now a pure count of premium rows, reproducible from model_usage_jsonl_row_count's premium subset alone.

dimensions.precedence_rule: Evaluate in this fixed order and stop at the first match: high, then moderate, then low. The three predicates are mutually exclusive by construction; a measurement never matches more than one.
dimensions.high: artifact_count strictly above 80, OR artifact_bytes_approx strictly above 5 MB, OR retry_count 2 or more. Checked first: this predicate overrides low/moderate even if the count/bytes alone would otherwise read as low.
dimensions.moderate: not high, AND (artifact_count is 51 to 80 inclusive, OR artifact_bytes_approx is strictly above 2 MB and at most 5 MB)
dimensions.low: not high and not moderate: artifact_count at or below 50 (5 files per scheduled run x the 10-run baseline: run_state.json, run_summary.json, signals.csv, submitted_orders.csv, plus one of filled_orders.csv/drift_report) AND artifact_bytes_approx at or below 2 MB
dimensions.note: The prior high predicate ('any single artifact path rewritten 2 or more times') is not observable from a persisted same-day artifact: this contract defines no write-history log or rewrite counter, and a report reading only final file contents/mtimes cannot tell a once-written file from a twice-rewritten one with identical final content. retry_count is the one already-required, already-persisted counter that reflects repeated rewrites in practice (a retry reuses and rewrites the same run directory's artifacts per the scheduled_run_artifact_contract's recovery_rerun convention), so it replaces the unobservable predicate rather than removing repeated-rewrite coverage entirely.

dimensions.precedence_rule: Evaluate in this fixed order and stop at the first match: high, then moderate, then low, mirroring artifact_load's precedence_rule so the predicates are mutually exclusive.
dimensions.high: error_count plus retry_count is 4 or more, OR any failed scheduled start (any failed_start_no_evidence record) occurred today. Checked first: a single failed scheduled start is high even when the count alone would read as moderate (e.g. count=1).
dimensions.moderate: not high: error_count plus retry_count is 1 to 3

proxy_bands.band_derivation_rule: Each reported band names the dimension, the observed proxy value, and the threshold it crossed, so the band is reproducible from the artifacts rather than asserted.

tasks.cron_recurrence_caveat: A 5-field cron expression has no year field, so 30 20 27 7 * recurs every July 27, not only in 2026, unless the external scheduler independently removes or disables this entry after it fires once -- codex review discussion_r3658332755. TWO script-side guards close the re-fire hole. (1) generate_report() content-gates itself to trading_day='2026-07-27' (SUPPORTED_TRADING_DAY) and raises for any other value. (2) Because the command below HARDCODES --trading-day 2026-07-27, guard (1) alone could never fire on a 2027 re-run -- the hardcoded argument satisfies it, and the run would re-read the 2026 artifact tree and overwrite the 2026 outputs -- so _main() additionally compares the ACTUAL America/New_York execution date and refuses (exit code 2, nothing written) when its calendar year differs from the trading day's; the year, not the exact date, so a legitimate same-year manual re-run still works -- codex review discussion_r3659140568. A deliberate later replay must pass --allow-execution-date-mismatch explicitly; the scheduler entry never does. The external scheduler side of this gap still requires either a scheduler-native one-shot trigger or a manual retirement step after 2026-07-27, since a cron field alone cannot express a single year -- but an unretired entry now fails closed instead of republishing over the real report.
tasks.command_note: Invoked as a module (python -m scripts.generate_credit_usage_proxy_report), not as a bare script path: direct execution (python scripts/generate_credit_usage_proxy_report.py) puts scripts/ rather than the repo root on sys.path, so the script's `from scripts.*` absolute imports raise ModuleNotFoundError before argument parsing -- codex review discussion_r3658332750. Run from the repository root (the external scheduler's working directory for every other command in this manifest). REWRITTEN 2026-08-02 (Codex review: "Keep the report command on the shared artifact root"): the command previously passed --cron-tracking-root/--json-out/--md-out with an explicit shell fallback, "${DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT:-/home/user/workspace/cron_tracking}" -- but dca_paths.cron_tracking_root() (which every other in-repo producer/consumer resolves its root through, including this script's own _default_cron_tracking_root()) falls back to a checkout-relative cron_tracking/ directory when the env var is unset, NOT that hardcoded literal. In an unconfigured checkout this command would therefore read/write a different tree than every other task, report real runs as missing, or write outputs outside the shared artifact tree. The new --write-defaults flag (scripts/generate_credit_usage_proxy_report.py) removes the shell-side root/path computation entirely: the script resolves cron-tracking-root via dca_paths.cron_tracking_root() and derives both output paths from default_report_paths(trading_day, cron_tracking_root) internally, so this command can never drift from the shared root the way a static shell fallback could. A deployment that sets $DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT still gets it honored automatically, exactly as before -- only the drift-prone hardcoded literal is gone.

Previously this entry had no cron_utc and no executable command at all -- codex review discussion_r3657271687 -- both gaps are now closed: cron_utc above, and scripts/generate_credit_usage_proxy_report.py is a real, tested script that reads persisted same-day artifacts and produces the six required_sections. EDT-months half of the paired month-end volatility risk schedule (EST half is 17a3b2a9); programmatic month-end trigger checks are disabled so both fire on days 25-31 and each self-gates on the final-eligible-market-day check. Notifies in-app and email only if the Notion refresh fails, data quality blocks the run, or one or more tickers triggered the 3x tier more than twice (email subject 'Month-end DCA volatility risk table'); no Slack. Full monthly volatility risk reporting lives here, not in daily execution tasks; the daily cost-saving operating mode is unchanged. See month_end_volatility_risk_policy.
